framing_assertion.rationale: The initial request from SH-REQ assumes carrier rejects of shipment notices (per DA-REJ) are due to fixable data errors that an AI agent can auto-correct and resubmit, which is itself an unverified causal claim.

hypotheses.statement: Carrier rejects recorded in DA-REJ are caused by correctable data errors in the shipment notices sent via H-1, so an AI agent can auto-fix and resubmit them successfully.
hypotheses.rationale: This is SH-REQ's framing underlying the request; if true it justifies building an auto-fix/resubmit agent as proposed, but it has not been verified against actual reject reasons.
discriminating_evidence: H-1 payload structure vs. notice fields flagged in rejects
Recurrence pattern of same error type across rejected notices

hypotheses.statement: Rejects are driven by legitimate carrier business rules (e.g. capacity, routing, embargo) rather than shipper data defects, so notices are not 'wrong' and should not be auto-modified.
hypotheses.rationale: DA-REJ is explicitly described as 'carrier business rejects', suggesting rejects may reflect policy decisions by ORG-B rather than data quality faults correctable by ORG-A's agent.
discriminating_evidence: Distribution of reject reason categories in DA-REJ (business-rule vs. data-error types)
SH-INT (interface owner, ORG-B) account of why rejects occur

hypotheses.statement: Errors causing rejects originate in ORG-A systems/data upstream of P-1 (shipment notice process), so fixing the outbound notice at resubmission time only masks a deeper source-system problem.
hypotheses.rationale: P-1 steps, actors, and systems are currently empty/unspecified, leaving open whether the defect enters before the notice is generated; an auto-fix-and-resubmit agent would not address a recurring upstream cause.
discriminating_evidence: Correlation of rejected notice fields to ORG-A source records (e.g. order/inventory data)

hypotheses.statement: A mapping or schema mismatch between ORG-A's and ORG-B's notice formats causes rejects despite H-1 being flagged technically VALID and HEALTHY, meaning the handoff's validity checks don't catch the actual failure mode.
hypotheses.rationale: H-1's semantic_validity=VALID and delivery_status=HEALTHY appear to contradict the existence of carrier rejects, implying the current validity check may not detect the condition actually causing rejection.
discriminating_evidence: Definition/scope of H-1 semantic_validity check vs. actual carrier reject criteria
Comparison of notice schema fields against ORG-B's acceptance rules

hypotheses.statement: The true scope and pattern of rejects cannot yet be established because DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN, so the problem may be mischaracterized based on a partial or unrepresentative sample.
hypotheses.rationale: DA-REJ's completeness field is explicitly UNKNOWN, so any root-cause claim built on it (including the requester's) carries unassessed uncertainty about coverage.
discriminating_evidence: Cross-check of reject count against total shipment notice volume sent via H-1

output.affected_process: P-1 shipment notice process (ORG-A → ORG-B via H-1)
output.root_problem: Shipment notices sent from ORG-A to ORG-B via handoff H-1 are being rejected by the carrier (logged in DA-REJ) because the notices themselves carry correctable content/data defects — unresolved location references (LOC_UNKNOWN) and out-of-order event data (EVENT_ORDER) — rather than because the carrier system is generically flaky (E-02) or because carrier business rules legitimately reject them (H-CARRIER-BUSINESS-RULE-REJECT, rejected).
output.requested_solution: Deploy an AI agent to automatically fix rejected shipment notices and resubmit them to the carrier.
symptoms: Shipment notices submitted via H-1 are rejected by the carrier, with sampled reject-log records tagged LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) (E-01, F-01).
The requester attributes rejects to generic carrier-system flakiness and proposes blanket resubmission, a claim that conflicts with the tool-derived reject-reason evidence (C-1, C-2).
causal_chain: ORG-A submits a shipment notice to carrier ORG-B through handoff H-1, which is flagged semantically VALID and HEALTHY at the transport level.
The notice content itself contains data defects in some fields: an unresolved/missing location reference in some notices and out-of-order event sequencing in others (E-01, F-01).
The carrier's intake processing rejects notices carrying these content defects and logs the reason (LOC_UNKNOWN or EVENT_ORDER) in DA-REJ (E-01, F-01).
Rejected notices remain stuck unprocessed until the content defect is corrected and the notice is resubmitted.

assumptions.statement: The 3-record reject sample in E-01 (2 LOC_UNKNOWN, 1 EVENT_ORDER) reflects the general reject pattern for shipment notices rather than an atypical slice.
LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER reject reasons can be algorithmically fixed without manual intervention and without introducing new errors.
H-1 being flagged semantically VALID and HEALTHY does not guarantee notice content is free of the defects actually causing rejects.

unknowns.question: What is the true distribution of reject reasons across the full population of rejected notices, given DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN and only 3 records have been reviewed?
unknowns.decision_impact: Determines whether auto-correction logic needs to cover more reject categories than LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER before scaling, or whether the current sample already captures the dominant pattern.
unknowns.resolution_path: Pull the complete or a statistically adequate sample of DA-REJ records and recompute the reject-reason breakdown.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Scope auto-correction only to the two confirmed reasons (LOC_UNKNOWN, EVENT_ORDER) until full visibility is established; route other reasons to manual review.

unknowns.question: Can LOC_UNKNOWN and EVENT_ORDER rejects actually be corrected deterministically without producing new, different rejects or data corruption?
unknowns.decision_impact: Determines whether auto-correct-and-resubmit can be enabled at all, or must stay human-reviewed per notice.
unknowns.resolution_path: Test correction logic against the sampled rejects (and a wider sample) and verify resubmission outcomes in DA-REJ before any unattended deployment.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Keep auto-corrected notices in a human-reviewed queue before resubmission until correction logic is validated against real reject outcomes.

unknowns.question: Is a schema/mapping mismatch between ORG-A's and ORG-B's notice formats (undetected by H-1's VALID/HEALTHY flags) contributing to the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER rejects?
unknowns.decision_impact: If a mapping mismatch is the real driver, fixing individual notice content would only treat symptoms; the handoff mapping itself would need correction.
unknowns.resolution_path: Compare ORG-A notice payload fields against ORG-B's expected schema/business rules for location and event-sequence data.
unknowns.safe_placeholder: Continue current manual correction process for notice content pending this comparison.

output.summary: The problem (PD-1) is that carrier rejects of shipment notices sent via H-1 (logged in DA-REJ) have an unestablished dominant cause: a reviewed 3-record sample (F-01/E-01) shows LOC_UNKNOWN (N-1, N-2) and EVENT_ORDER (N-3) tags, but DA-REJ completeness is UNKNOWN, so it is unclear if this generalizes (H-INCOMPLETE-REJECT-VISIBILITY). The requester SH-REQ proposed two conflicting framings — auto-fix-and-resubmit (CL-01) and 'carrier system is flaky, just resubmit' (CL-02/E-02) — which conflict with E-01 and with each other (C-1, C-2). The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two critical/high unknowns to open verification obligations (VOB-U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS, VOB-U-REJECT-REASON-DISTRIBUTION). The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no items held, because solution_design SD-1 lists resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1 in release_scope/minimum_useful_scope, yet its own narrative says release_scope is 'currently empty' and that this action is withheld under remedy SR-ENFORCE-VOB-GATING-ON-CORREC — a documented contradiction between structured scope and narrative that verification flagged (semantic:release_scope_vs_withholding_consistency failed at seq 84) but did not block release. No mutating action was actually executable this cycle: only the read-only reject-log tool is in the tool_surface, and both VOBs remain OPEN, so query_full_reject_log, classify_reject_reasons, and correct_notice_content stay blocked, and resubmission is withheld per the recorded remedy despite not being formally named in either VOB's blocking_scope.
key_points: Root problem per PD-1: dominant reject reason for H-1 shipment notices is unestablished; sample evidence (F-01/E-01) shows LOC_UNKNOWN x2, EVENT_ORDER x1 out of only 3 records against a DA-REJ population of unknown completeness.

Two stakeholder-driven, conflicting hypotheses exist: CL-01 (auto-fix and resubmit) and CL-02 (carrier is flaky, just resubmit); E-02 (CL-02's basis) is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that conflicts with the authoritative tool evidence E-01 (conflicts C-1, C-2).
DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS (seq 51), deferring U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS (CRITICAL) and U-REJECT-REASON-DISTRIBUTION (HIGH) to VOBs that remain OPEN.

Release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with an empty hold list (seq 88); nothing was held back formally even though the practical effect is that no corrective or resubmission action executes this cycle.

Verification found a semantic inconsistency (seq 84): solution_design.release_scope/minimum_useful_scope name resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1 as released, while the design's unfinished_scope narrative says release_scope is empty and this action is withheld via remedy SR-ENFORCE-VOB-GATING-ON-CORREC.

Both open VOBs block query_full_reject_log:DA-REJ, classify_reject_reasons:DA-REJ, and correct_notice_content:H-1; resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1 is not named in either VOB's blocking_scope but is withheld anyway per the recorded remedy to avoid repeating failures from blind resubmission.
The tool_surface for this scenario contains only the read-only reject-log tool, consistent with the fact that no mutating/correction/resubmission action is reported as executed.

Two assumptions remain unverified: A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS (3-record sample assumed not an outlier batch) and A-TAG-MEANING (LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER assumed to reflect genuine content defects, not carrier-side artifacts), both resting on evidence E-01.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning critical open questions were deferred into tracked verification obligations (VOBs) rather than resolved before proceeding.

A verification check (semantic:release_scope_vs_withholding_consistency) found a direct contradiction: the structured release_scope/minimum_useful_scope fields list resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1 as released, while the design's own text says release_scope is empty and that action is withheld.

VOB-U-REJECT-LOG-COMPLETENESS is still OPEN, so whether DA-REJ's reject log is complete or just a partial/filtered view is unresolved, and this blocks query_full_reject_log and correct_notice_content.

VOB-U-REJECT-REASON-DISTRIBUTION is still OPEN, so whether LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER are actually the dominant reject reasons across the full population is unresolved, blocking classify_reject_reasons and correct_notice_content.

The findings rest on only a 3-record sample (M-SAMPLE-SIZE-REVIEWED=3) from DA-REJ, which may not generalize to the full reject population since DA-REJ's completeness status for this analysis was UNKNOWN.

A structural gap exists: both open VOBs list as their own blocking_scope the very diagnostic actions (query_full_reject_log, classify_reject_reasons) that would be needed to resolve them, leaving release_scope effectively empty.

resubmit_shipment_notice:H-1 is withheld as a precaution per remedy SR-ENFORCE-VOB-GATING-ON-CORREC, even though it is not formally listed in either VOB's blocking_scope, because resubmitting without first resolving whether rejects are content defects or carrier flakiness risks repeating failures.

Two assumptions underlying the analysis (A-SAMPLE-REPRESENTATIVENESS and A-TAG-MEANING) are unverified and depend on full-population data from DA-REJ and clarification from stakeholder SH-INT (interface owner) on what the LOC_UNKNOWN/EVENT_ORDER tags actually mean.
